items.text: A scheme over $k$ = a scheme $X$ with a morphism $X\to S=\operatorname{Spec}k$.
$X$ is a sheaf for the Zariski topology (covering families = open immersions covering $Y$).
A sheaf on $\mathrm{Sch}/k$ is known by its values on affine schemes: cover $Y$ by affine $Y_i$, $Y_{ij}$ by affine $Y_{ijk}$ ($X_f$ form a basis, open subsets of schemes are schemes).
A scheme is a functor on commutative rings with extra properties; $S$ = the functor represented by $k$.
$X=\coprod X_i$: sum of the topological spaces with $\mathcal O_X|_{X_i}=\mathcal O_{X_i}$; it is the sum in ringed spaces, in locally ringed spaces and in schemes.

A morphism $S'\to X$: a decomposition $S'=\coprod S'_i$ into open sets and morphisms $S'_i\to X_i$. $\coprod\operatorname{Hom}(S',X_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}(S',X)$ is not bijective, but is after sheafification.

Sum of sheaves: (a) $\alpha_i\colon\widetilde X_i\to\widetilde X$ monomorphisms; (b) $\widetilde X_i\times_{\widetilde X}\widetilde X_j=\varnothing$ ($i\neq j$); (c) the $\widetilde X_i$ cover $\widetilde X$.
